title: Pop-Up Distractions Reveal Bag-of-Events Behavior in Video Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2605.27101v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: A key capability for video understanding is reliably linking subjects to events across time, yet whether Video Large Language Models (VideoLLMs) actually achieve this remains unclear. In this work, we introduce DistractionBench to evaluate whether VideoLLMs can robustly link subjects and events in the presence of unrelated video segments. Through controlled interventions, such as inserting short advertisement clips into longer videos, we show that VideoLLMs frequently hallucinate interactions between entities from different segments, incorrectly attributing actions from injected advertisements to subjects in the main video. We characterize this systematic hallucination as bag-of-events (BoE) behavior, where models process videos as collections of events rather than temporally structured sequences. translated_title: 弹出干扰揭示视频大型语言模型中的“事件袋”行为
translated_abstract: arXiv:2605.27101v2 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：视频理解的一个关键能力是可靠地将主体与跨时间的事件关联起来，然而视频大型语言模型（VideoLLMs）是否真正实现这一点仍不清楚。在本工作中，我们引入了DistractionBench来评估VideoLLMs在存在无关视频片段时是否能稳健地将主体和事件关联起来。通过受控干预，例如在较长的视频中插入短广告片段，我们展示了VideoLLMs经常幻觉化地产生来自不同片段实体之间的交互，错误地将注入广告中的动作归因于主视频中的主体。我们将这种系统性幻觉特征化为“事件袋”（BoE）行为，即模型将视频视为事件的集合而非时间上结构化的序列。评估了11种流行的VideoLLMs，我们发现所有模型都表现出显著的BoE行为。我们的发现表明VideoLLMs缺乏时间结构化的视频理解能力。
tldr: 这项研究通过引入DistractionBench测试，发现所有视频大型语言模型普遍存在将无关事件错误关联的“事件袋”幻觉行为，缺乏跨时间关联主体与事件的稳健能力。
en_tdlr: This study introduces DistractionBench and reveals that all video large language models exhibit systematic "bag-of-events" hallucination, failing to robustly link subjects and events across time.
